chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: Grandpaw of the jazz, and not an artist
summary: Smith is introduced as the grandfather of Dallas jazz, enjoys hearing young players, and says he is just one in the bunch.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: But coming back to the music, do you to any extent feel that by being a Jazz musician, and a very good Jazz musician too...
...that you helped contribute to creating something which is unique, something which is artistic, something which some people say is the only American art form.
Do you feel proud of that at all?
Well...in a way, yeah, I do. I'm supposed to be
out (?) tonight at the (?) Room, but I don't think I'm going. But they say I helped a lot... Every time I get out there, they announce that I'm the grandpaw of the Jazz here.

Yeah. Say, "Here's the grandpaw of the Jazz, the one that started a lot of the musicians that play," and this, which and whatnot, and going on... Well, they always give me that credit. Well, it's all right. But I like to see them guys play. I like to hear 'em play. Like I was telling the boys all night, "It makes me feel good..." Which it does. It makes me feel good that them guys come on and playing such a nice horn with a good tone, as well as running up and down his horn, and learn that technique of how to play something and make it sound like something, and it's pleasing to everybody's ear. And it makes me feel good. It lets him do it. I don't do it any more...
Do you consider yourself an artist? Do you think you're an artist?
Do you think that you are an artist? Do you think of yourself as being an artist?
Oh, no. No. I think I'm just one in the bunch. Just one of those old scalawags in the bunch! Ha-ha! Yeah, that's all.
